lines:
IMPLEMENTED.

`restore_frozen_mcp` (service/tool_plugins.rs) now returns `RestoredFrozenMcpV1` { manifests, definitions }: after opening the Chat's frozen endpoints it builds each bound MCP tool's model-facing definition from the live session catalog — capability id, provider alias rebuilt via `mcp_provider_name` from the Chat's own frozen server label, live description and `input_schema`. The schema-equality rejection is removed.

`complete_workflow_input` (service.rs) applies those definitions onto `execution_request.tools` for the pass, so `freeze_mcp_binding` re-derives the MCP limit's `schema_hash` from the live schema and the provider is offered the current interface, while authority (server set, tool ids, configuration, approval class, credential binding) stays frozen. The separate `restore_frozen_mcp` reconnect calls on approval/question resume keep working and no longer reject on metadata drift.

Boundary kept: a tool the server no longer advertises is a missing capability, so it fails closed with an accurate reason ("MCP tool '<id>' is no longer provided by server '<server>'") instead of the conflated schema message.

Out of scope (unchanged): binding a brand-new MCP tool or server mid-Chat; that still needs a New Chat and belongs to a separate task with live discovery for unattested capabilities.

Tests added in service/tests/question.rs, sharing the MCP fixture: `a_changed_mcp_tool_interface_is_adopted_for_the_chat` (live schema adopted, provider alias and manifests kept), `an_mcp_tool_the_server_no_longer_provides_still_fails_closed`, and `a_changed_mcp_interface_reaches_the_next_pass_without_a_new_chat` (an enqueue after the server edit is accepted and its preflighted request carries the live schema).

VERIFICATION
cargo test --lib: 508 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. The `question::` filter run: 17 passed (14 pre-existing + 3 new), including the existing `answering_a_question_reconnects_the_chats_frozen_mcp_endpoints`.
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check on tool_plugins.rs and tests/question.rs: clean.
Note: this sandbox shells out without HOME, so the fixture runtime needed HOME=/tmp/aworkit-test-home for skill-home resolution; that is environmental, not a code change.

Not verified: the native desktop smoke (needs a rebuilt Tauri binary + WebView), and the in-process case where a server is edited while the same application generation keeps a cached MCP snapshot — with a reused cached snapshot the frozen and live schema already agree, so no lockout occurred there either.

A resumed Chat failed with "MCP schema changed for 'mcp://.../adashi_help'; start a New Chat to use the new definition" after the MCP server was edited. `restore_frozen_mcp` compared every bound MCP tool's frozen `input_schema` with the live catalog and failed the whole pass on any difference, which contradicts the snapshot_freezer "Existing Chat continuation" rule: an improved tool replaces its previous behaviour for existing Chats, and installed metadata differences must not lock a Chat out.

Task 107 flagged this as an explicit follow-up (its memo item 2: "restore_frozen_mcp still rejects an MCP schema change for an existing Chat, which the design says must not lock a Chat out because installed metadata differs").

Scope:
1. `restore_frozen_mcp` reconnects the Chat's frozen endpoints and returns both the manifests and the live model-facing definition of every bound MCP tool (capability id, provider alias rebuilt from the Chat's frozen server label, live description and input_schema).
2. `complete_workflow_input` applies those definitions to the pass's tool bindings, so the re-derived schema hash and provider-visible interface come from this generation's session while authority (server set, tool ids, approval/credential binding) stays frozen.
3. A tool the server no longer advertises is a missing capability, not metadata drift, so it still fails closed with an accurate reason.

Out of scope: binding a brand-new MCP tool or server mid-Chat (still refused; needs its own task and live discovery for unattested capabilities).

data.title: Adopt a changed MCP tool interface for an existing Chat instead of locking it out
